s1.syndrome_frame: Syndromic pigmentary retinal dystrophy with systemic features
salient_findings: Intellectual disability with appropriate social behavior
key_facts: Bilateral cataract extraction with 13D monofocal intraocular lenses 3 years earlier
Transient neutropenia in childhood that resolved spontaneously
Joint hyperextensibility of the hands, feet, ankles, and knees
Best-corrected visual acuity was 2/10 in each eye
Fundus examination showed bilateral disc pallor, generalized arteriolar narrowing, mid-peripheral bone-spicule pigmentary changes, and retinal pigment epithelium atrophy

differentials: Cerebroretinal microangiopathy with calcifications and cysts
per_call: Cerebroretinal microangiopathy with calcifications and cysts

shortlist.label: Bardet-Biedl syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Syndromic pigmentary retinal dystrophy with systemic features, including intellectual disability, obesity, and joint hyperextensibility

shortlist.label: Cohen syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Pigmentary retinal dystrophy, intellectual disability, and microcephaly, with possible myopia and joint hyperextensibility

shortlist.label: Alstrom syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Syndromic pigmentary retinal dystrophy with systemic features, including obesity, intellectual disability, and possible myopia

shortlist.label: Senior-Loken syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Pigmentary retinal dystrophy with renal involvement, possible intellectual disability, and systemic features

shortlist.label: Usher syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Pigmentary retinal dystrophy with hearing loss, possible intellectual disability, and systemic features

raw.rationale: The combination of severe rod-cone retinal dystrophy, high bilateral myopia, intellectual disability, microcephaly, and distinct facial features such as a thick head of hair, bushy eyebrows, and a short upturned philtrum are characteristic of Cohen syndrome.

rejected.label: Bardet-Biedl syndrome
rejected.why: Typically associated with polydactyly, hypogonadism, and renal abnormalities, which are not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Alstrom syndrome
rejected.why: Characterized by obesity, diabetes, and hearing loss, which are not prominent features in this case.

rejected.label: Senior-Loken syndrome
rejected.why: Primarily associated with nephronophthisis, which is not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Usher syndrome
rejected.why: Typically involves hearing loss, which is not mentioned in the vignette, and does not fully account for the range of systemic features described.
